plants.name: Prunus × yedoensis
plants.description: Clouds of pale, almond-scented blossoms cover bare branches before the leaves appear. Petals fall like soft snow in the spring breeze. The display draws crowds for flower-viewing picnics.
plants.bloomingSeason: Mid-March to mid-April, depending on latitude. Peak bloom comes in late March in warmer areas. Early blooms can appear in mid-March in the southern and warmer parts of Japan.
plants.location: Southern and western Japan, such as Kyushu and Shikoku, where early blooms begin around mid-March. It is also planted widely in temperate cities around the world.
plants.funFact: Yoshino cherries are a cultivated hybrid. Nearly all of them descend from a single original tree and are propagated by grafting, so trees across a region often bloom in near-perfect sync.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: Nodding golden trumpets surrounded by paler yellow petals light up woodland floors and meadows. Whole drifts can appear almost overnight. They are a cheerful sign that winter is ending.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late February through March, often peaking in mid-March in milder parts of its range.
plants.location: Western Europe, including the woodlands and meadows of southern and western England and Wales.
plants.funFact: The plant makes toxic alkaloids, including galantamine. Galantamine has been developed into a medicine used to treat symptoms of Alzheimer's disease.

plants.name: Magnolia campbellii
plants.description: Huge goblet-shaped flowers open on leafless branches. They are among the most dramatic blooms of early spring. Each blossom can be as wide as a dinner plate.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late February to March in the Himalayan foothills and in mild temperate gardens.
plants.location: The Himalayan foothills of Nepal, Bhutan, and northeast India. It is also grown in mild gardens in Cornwall, Ireland, and New Zealand.
plants.funFact: Magnolias are among the most ancient flowering plants. Their blooms look much like early flowers that were pollinated by beetles before bees became common.
